title: Ozone slopes were uncertain after collection-month control in six exposed-anther herbarium samples from 1941 to 2017
abstract: We tested the link between total-column ozone and floral UV pigmentation in 934 exposed-anther herbarium specimens. Six tests covered Australia, Eurasia and North America in 1941-1985 and 1986-2017. Models controlled species-specific collection months and time trends, monthly temperature and location. All six family-wise 95% intervals included zero. Ozone slopes ranged from -4.14 to +1.41 percentage points of UV-absorbing petal area per +10 Dobson units. Month controls removed 64-91% of the exposure variation left by the other controls. Equal-species weights and a transformed response gave the same slope signs, but did not give clear effects. These tests use disjoint specimens from one archive, not new independent archives. Few species, nonrandom collection, source exposure estimates and unmodeled shared errors limit inference. The results do not establish an ozone effect or its absence. Total-column ozone differs from surface ozone pollution. The package includes code, a specimen panel, source hashes, selection records, numerical checks and retrieval instructions.

display.caption: Ozone slopes for six region-period samples. Blue points use species-specific month intercepts and time trends. Bars use species clusters and a six-test family-wise correction. Orange crosses omit month cells. All intervals include zero. Units are percentage points of UV-absorbing petal area per +10 Dobson units.
